hub_subtitle: Business English para seguros, reuniões e entrevistas — e o desbloqueio da fala, do primeiro dia ao último

lesson.menu_title: What Happened? What Didn't Happen? -- The Past in the Negative, and the Zurich Interview
lesson.menu_desc: A aula em que a Paula descobre que a história dela não é só o que aconteceu — é também o que não aconteceu. Na aula 14 ela contou a carreira no afirmativo (I began, I got, I became, I made). Hoje ela aprende as duas peças que faltavam: didn't pra negar e Did you…? pra perguntar — e a regra de ouro que assusta e depois alivia: depois de didn't e de did, o verbo volta a ficar pelado (I didn't go, nunca I didn't went). O passado já está no did; o verbo não precisa repetir. O cenário é a entrevista da Zurich, um ano atrás: ela não se candidatou, ela não dormiu na véspera, e a banca não perguntou sobre o inglês dela. Seis palavras novas (interview, apply, hire, offer, decide, nervous), o Greg fazendo as perguntas de verdade numa call, e a Sofia contando, do outro lado da mesa, por que contrataram a Paula. -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 15 -- What Happened? What Didn't Happen?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Paula Morales | Lesson 15 -- What Happened? What Didn't Happen?
lesson.grammar_point: past simple negative and questions -- didn't + bare verb for the negative, and Did you...? / What did you...? for yes-no and wh questions

listenings.text: Hi, Paula. David here. Today you are going to learn the small word that changes everything in the past, and it is didn't. Before your lesson, let me tell you what I didn't do. Ten years ago, a big company in Chicago called me for an interview. I didn't apply for that job. They found me. And here is my confession. The night before, I didn't sleep. Not one hour. I was nervous, and I made a long list of hard words in English, because I thought they were going to test my grammar. Then I sat down in that room, and they didn't ask about my grammar. They didn't ask about my list. They asked one question. Tell us about a problem you solved. So I told them a story about a client, in simple words, with many mistakes, and they hired me two days later. I didn't win that job with perfect English, Paula. I won it with a real story. Remember one thing today. After didn't, the verb goes back to normal. I didn't sleep. I didn't apply. Never I didn't slept. The past is already inside the word didn't, so the verb does not repeat it. That is the whole rule. See you soon.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here. Last year I was in the room when you came for your interview at Zurich, and today I want to tell you what happened on our side of the table, because I don't think you know. First, you didn't apply for that job. We called you. A broker in Sao Paulo said your name to me, and I looked for you. Second, you arrived early, and you were nervous. I saw it. Your hands were nervous, but your voice was not. You talked about large risks for twenty minutes and you didn't stop once. And now the part I really want you to hear. We didn't ask about your English. Not one question. Two of the people at that table asked me later, is her English good? And I said, I don't know, and it is not the reason we want her. We hired you because you know the work, and because you didn't pretend. When you didn't have a number, you said, I will check and come back. Do you know how rare that is? So today, when you learn didn't, think about this. You didn't get this job because you were perfect. You got it because you were honest, and you did not stop. See you Monday, Paula.

items.situation: Greg asks if you applied for the Zurich job. You didn't -- they called you. Tell him, in a full sentence.
tips: I didn't apply. They called me.
No, I didn't apply for the job -- Sofia called me.

items.situation: A colleague asks if you slept well before the interview. You didn't sleep at all. Say it.
tips: I didn't sleep the night before.
No, I didn't sleep -- I was too nervous.

items.situation: You want to ask Greg about his first interview at Zurich. Ask him if he was nervous.
tips: Did you feel nervous in your first interview?
Greg, did you get nervous in your interview?

items.situation: The panel asked about your career, not about your English. Tell a friend what they did not ask.
tips: They didn't ask about my English.
They asked about my career -- they didn't ask about my English.

items.situation: Ask a colleague about the offer: you want to know when the company made it.
tips: When did they make you an offer?
When did the company offer you the job?

items.situation: Greg asks if you decided on the same day. You didn't -- you took a week. Answer him.
tips: No, I didn't decide that day. I took one week.
I didn't decide immediately -- I thought about it for a week.

bank.label: Saying what did NOT happen / Dizer o que NÃO aconteceu
items: I didn't apply -- they called me.
I didn't sleep the night before.
They didn't ask about my English.
I didn't have the number, so I checked first.

Did they offer you the position?
